p.src: Now Song Gongming, after attacking Dongping once and Dongchang twice, returned to the stronghold. When he counted the leaders of every rank and found that they numbered one hundred and eight in all, he was overjoyed and said to his brothers, “Ever since I caused the disturbance at Jiangzhou and came up the mountain, I have relied upon the heroic aid of you, my brothers, who made me your chief. Now that all one hundred and eight leaders have gathered together, my heart is filled with joy. Since our elder brother Chao Gai departed this life, whenever we have led our forces forth and returned to the mountain, we have all come safely home. This is the protection of Heaven, not something within human power! Though some were captured and cast into bonds, or returned after suffering wounds, all are now safe and sound. Today all one hundred and eight of us are assembled here; truly, such a thing has seldom been seen from ancient times to the present. Wherever our weapons have passed, living creatures have been slain, and we have made no rites of atonement. I therefore wish to hold a grand Daoist Offering to the All-Encompassing Heaven, to repay the favor of Heaven, Earth, and the divine powers for their protection: first, to pray that all our brothers may enjoy peace in body and mind; second, to pray that the court will soon bestow its gracious favor and pardon our grave crime of defying Heaven, whereupon we shall devote all our strength, sacrifice our lives, and serve the nation loyally until death; and third, to commend the Heavenly King Chao to an early rebirth in the celestial realm, so that through life after life we may meet him again, and also to deliver all those who died untimely or cruel deaths, by fire or drowning, and every innocent person who was killed, that they may all attain a blessed path. I wish to undertake this matter, but I do not know what you brothers think of it.” All the leaders declared, “This is a virtuous and worthy deed. Our elder brother’s judgment is sound.” Wu Yong then said, “First ask Gongsun Sheng, Master Yiqing, to preside over the Offering. Then send men down the mountain to invite accomplished Daoist adepts from far and wide, bringing their ritual vessels to the stronghold. Others should purchase all the necessary incense, candles, paper horses, flowers, fruit, offerings, vegetarian dishes, pure food, and every other required article.” After deliberation, they chose the fifteenth day of the fourth month to begin the meritorious rite, which would last seven days and nights. The stronghold distributed money lavishly and pressed forward with the preparations. As the appointed date drew near, four long streamers were hung before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, and a three-tiered high altar was erected inside. Within the hall were installed sacred images of the Three Pure Ones adorned with the Seven Treasures; in ordered ranks were set the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions, the Twelve Zodiacal Palaces, and all the star officials and divine sovereigns presiding over the Offering. Outside the hall stood the guardian generals of the altar, Cui, Lu, Deng, and Dou. When all had been arranged, the ritual vessels were set out in full, and the invited Daoists numbered forty-nine together with Gongsun Sheng. p.src: Incense smoke rose in auspicious clouds, and flowers clustered around embroidered screens. A thousand painted candles streamed with light, and hundreds of silver lamps scattered their radiance. Pairs of feathered canopies were raised on high, while rank upon rank of banners and streamers stood densely arrayed. A pure breeze bore through the Three Realms the chanting of the Pacing the Void hymn; beneath the chill moon, celestial night vapor descended from the Nine Heavens. When the golden bell was struck, the High Celebrant presented his memorial to the Sovereign of the Void; when jade pendants chimed, the Chief Precentor mounted the altar to pay court to the Jade Emperor. On crimson gauze robes the stars shone resplendent; lotus crowns gleamed gold and azure, adding majesty. The divine generals guarding the altar looked fearsome, and the duty officers of merit were valiant. The Daoists recited the precious litany in unison and ascended the Jasper Terrace to pour water and offer flowers; the Perfected One intoned the sacred scripture in secret, held the ritual sword, and paced the stellar pattern of the Dipper. Dimly, an azure dragon came along the Yellow Way; lightly, white cranes descended from the Purple Court.

p.src: That day, Gongsun Sheng and the forty-eight Daoists performed the Offering in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. They held three services daily until the rites concluded on the seventh day. Song Jiang sought a response from Heaven and specifically ordered Gongsun Sheng to compose and offer a green memorial to the Celestial Emperor at each of the three daily services. At the third watch on the seventh night, Gongsun Sheng stood on the first tier of the Altar of the Sovereign of the Void, the Daoists on the second tier, and Song Jiang and the other leaders on the third, while the lesser chiefs, officers, and commanders all stood below the altar. All implored High Heaven, earnestly begging for a manifest response. At the third watch that night, they suddenly heard a sound in the heavens like silk being torn, directly above the Gate of Heaven in the northwest, the direction of Qian. When the people looked up, they saw a golden disk standing upright, pointed at both ends and broad in the middle. This is called “the opening of Heaven’s Gate,” and also “the opening of Heaven’s Eye.” From within it, fine rays dazzled the eyes and rosy clouds coiled all around. Out of its center rolled a mass of fire shaped like a great basket, tumbling straight down toward the Altar of the Sovereign of the Void. p.src: For the moment, Song Jiang ordered the paper offerings burned to conclude the rites. At daybreak, he gave the Daoists a vegetarian feast and presented each of them with gold and silk as an honorarium. Only then did they bring out the stone tablet for examination. Upon it were dragon figures, phoenix seals, and tadpole script, which no one could read. Among the Daoists was a man surnamed He, whose religious name was Xuantong. He said to Song Jiang, “My humble family possesses an old manuscript handed down by our ancestors that is specifically used to decipher celestial writing. Such writing has always been composed in tadpole characters, and so this poor Daoist is well able to recognize them. Once I translate them, we shall know the truth.” Song Jiang was delighted to hear this. He hurriedly held out the stone tablet and asked Daoist He to examine it. After studying it for a long while, the Daoist said, “This stone is engraved throughout with the illustrious names of the righteous warriors. On one side are the four characters ‘Carry Out the Way on Heaven’s Behalf,’ and on the other the four characters ‘Complete in Loyalty and Righteousness.’ At the top are the constellations of the Southern and Northern Dippers; and below them are the honorific titles. If I am not to be blamed for revealing them, I shall expound them one by one from the beginning.” Song Jiang said, “It is our good fortune that an eminent master has dispelled our confusion. Our affinity with you is indeed profound, and I am deeply grateful for the great kindness of your instruction. As for your fear of incurring Heaven’s blame, please conceal nothing. I beg you to reveal everything fully and not omit a single word.” Song Jiang summoned Xiao Rang, the Sacred-Handed Scholar, and had him transcribe the words onto yellow paper. Daoist He explained that the front bore thirty-six lines of celestial writing, all belonging to the Stars of the Heavenly Spirits; the back likewise bore seventy-two lines of celestial writing, all belonging to the Stars of the Earthly Fiends, with the names of the righteous warriors inscribed beneath. After examining the tablet for a long while, he had Xiao Rang copy everything upon it from beginning to end. p.src: Leaving aside the Taoist priests, who returned home, let us speak only of Song Jiang, who conferred with the strategists Wu the Scholar, Zhu Wu, and the others. They decided to erect a plaque in the hall bearing the three large characters “Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness,” and to replace the great plaque on the Pavilion of Severed Gold as well. At the front they established three passes, while behind the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness they built a Wild Goose Terrace, with a main hall at its summit and two rooms each on the east and west sides. The spirit tablet of the Heavenly King Chao was enshrined in the main hall. The eastern rooms housed Song Jiang, Wu Yong, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng; the western rooms, Lu Junyi, Gongsun Sheng, Kong Ming, and Kong Liang. In the row of rooms on the left of the second slope were Zhu Wu, Huang Xin, Sun Li, Xiao Rang, and Pei Xuan; in the row on the right were Dai Zong, Yan Qing, Zhang Qing, An Daoquan, and Huangfu Duan. To the left of the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, Chai Jin, Li Ying, Jiang Jing, and Ling Zhen were placed in charge of receiving and issuing money and provisions from the granaries; to the right were Hua Rong, Fan Rui, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun. At the first pass on the southern road before the mountain, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao stood guard; at the second pass, Lu Zhishen and Wu Song; and at the third pass, Zhu Tong and Lei Heng. The eastern mountain pass was guarded by Shi Jin and Liu Tang; the western mountain pass by Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu; and the northern mountain pass by Mu Hong and Li Kui. Beyond the six passes, eight stockades were established: four on land and four on the water. The due-south land stockade was assigned to Qin Ming, Suo Chao, Ou Peng, and Deng Fei; the due-east land stockade to Guan Sheng, Xu Ning, Xuan Zan, and Hao Siwen; the due-west land stockade to Lin Chong, Dong Ping, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo; and the due-north land stockade to Huyan Zhuo, Yang Zhi, Han Tao, and Peng Qi. The southeastern water stockade was assigned to Li Jun and Ruan Xiao'er; the southwestern water stockade to Zhang Heng and Zhang Shun; the northeastern water stockade to Ruan Xiaowu and Tong Wei; and the northwestern water stockade to Ruan Xiaoqi and Tong Meng. All the others were likewise assigned their respective duties.

p.src: New standards and banners of every kind were made, and at the mountaintop an apricot-yellow banner was raised, bearing the four words “Enforce Justice on Heaven’s Behalf.” Before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness stood two red embroidered banners: one read “Shandong’s Protector of Righteousness,” and the other “Hebei’s Jade Qilin.” Outside were banners of soaring dragons and tigers, flying bears and leopards, azure dragons and white tigers, vermilion birds and dark warriors, together with yellow battle-axes, white yak-tail standards, blue pennons, black canopies, scarlet tassels, and black command flags; besides the central army’s weapons and equipment, there were banners of the Four Measures and Five Directions, the Three Powers and Nine Luminaries, the Twenty-Eight Mansions, the Sixty-Four Hexagrams, the cosmic Nine Palaces and Eight Trigrams, and one hundred and twenty-four Heaven-Guarding banners. All of them were made by Hou Jian. Jin Dajian cast the military tallies and official seals. When all was ready, they chose an auspicious day and hour, slaughtered oxen and horses, offered sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, and the gods, hung the plaques for the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and the Pavilion of Severed Gold, and raised the apricot-yellow banner proclaiming “Enforce Justice on Heaven’s Behalf.”

p.src: From the eight quarters they shared one realm; though bearing different surnames, they formed one family. Heaven and earth revealed the essences of the Guiding Stars and Baleful Stars; the human world united all the finest gifts of heroic spirits. Though a thousand leagues apart, they seemed to meet morning and night; with hearts united to the last inch, they could share life and death. In features and speech, north, south, east, and west all differed; Yet in heart and courage, loyalty, sincerity, faith, and honor knew no difference. Among them were scions of emperors and descendants of gods, wealthy men, generals, and officials, followers of the Three Teachings and every walk of life, even hunters and fishermen, butchers and executioners; all alike called one another brother, with no distinction between high and low; There were also brothers of one blood, matched husbands and wives, uncles and nephews, brothers-in-law, as well as masters and servants who had followed one another, and even former foes locked in bitter strife; yet all rejoiced alike at the wine feast, without regard for closeness or estrangement. Some were clever, some rough, some rustic and simple, some elegant and refined; never did these differences hinder them, for each lived true to his nature among the rest. Some excelled with brush or tongue, some with sword or spear, some at swift riding, some at theft and trickery; each possessed a special gift, and truly each was employed according to his talent. What was regrettable was their sham literary polish; having no choice, they installed a “Masterful Scholar” to preserve some semblance of elegance. Most vexing were the grand scholar’s caps; happily, they had first slain the White-Robed Scholar and washed away every trace of pedantic stinginess. Their domain spanned four or five hundred leagues, and their heroes numbered one hundred and eight. Formerly, one always heard their names spoken throughout the rivers and lakes, spreading peal after peal like the bell of an ancient tower; Only today was it known that their surnames stood arrayed among the stars, each linked to the next like beads upon a rosary. Chao Gai perhaps dared too much in calling himself king, and so departed this world early; only Song Jiang was willing to summon the host in defense of honor and take command of the stronghold. Say not that they merely gathered with wild cries in the mountain forests; long had they yearned to look toward and depend upon the imperial court.

p.src: Once the commands had been established in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness at Liangshan Marsh, every man obeyed them. Song Jiang chose an auspicious day and hour, burned a censer of incense, and had the drums sounded to summon everyone to the hall. Song Jiang addressed them: “Things are no longer as they once were. I have a few words to say. Now that the Stars of the Heavenly Guides and Earthly Luminaries have assembled, we must swear an oath before Heaven: let none harbor a divided heart; let us entrust life and death to one another, support one another through hardship and peril, and together defend the realm and bring peace to the people.” Everyone rejoiced. After each man had offered incense, they all knelt together in the hall. Song Jiang led them in the oath, saying: “I, Song Jiang, am but a lowly, insignificant clerk, unlearned and incapable. Yet I have received Heaven and Earth’s sheltering embrace and felt the light of sun and moon; I have gathered brothers on Liangshan and joined heroes at the marsh, one hundred and eight men in all, corresponding above to Heaven’s numbers and below to the hearts of men. From this day forth, should any man harbor an inhumane heart or sever himself from the great cause of righteousness, may Heaven and Earth strike him down and gods and men alike destroy him; may he never again be born in human form through ten thousand generations, but sink forever into the final calamity for countless ages. May we preserve loyalty and righteousness together in our hearts and together win meritorious renown for the realm. May we carry out Heaven’s Way, protect the land, and bring peace to the people. May the gods of Heaven bear witness, and may retribution be made manifest.” When the oath was finished, all voiced the same wish: that they might meet in life after life, encounter one another in age after age, and never be parted or hindered. That day they smeared their lips with blood and swore their covenant, then drank their fill before dispersing. p.src: The initial assignments having been settled, there is no need to repeat the matter. Now the heroes in the marsh, whenever they had leisure, would descend the mountain—some taking troops and horses, others setting out along their own routes with only a few leaders. If on the road they encountered merchants, carts, travelers, or horses, they let them pass freely; but if it was an official traveling to take up a post and they found gold or silver in his chests, they spared none of his household. Whatever they seized was sent to the stronghold and deposited in the treasury for common use, while trifling articles were divided among them as they pleased. Whether a hundred leagues away, two hundred, or three, if there was a great household that had amassed grain and wealth while harming the people, they openly led men there and carried everything up the mountain—who dared oppose them? Whenever they learned of some petty villain who had suddenly grown rich by oppressing decent folk and amassed a little property, no matter how near or far, they sent men at once to sweep it all up and bring it to the mountain. Such deeds, great and small, occurred in far more than a thousand places. Because no one could withstand them—and they cared nothing even if you cried your grievance to Heaven—these affairs never came to light, and so there is no tale to tell of them.

p.src: Yue He was singing this lyric, and had just reached the line, “May the Son of Heaven soon send down an edict offering amnesty,” when Wu Song cried, “Amnesty today, amnesty tomorrow—you will chill the hearts of all our brothers!” The Black Whirlwind opened his strange eyes wide and roared, “Amnesty, amnesty—what damned amnesty!” With a single kick he sent the table flying and smashed it to splinters. Song Jiang thundered, “How dare this black brute behave with such insolence? Men, drag him out and report to me when you have beheaded him!” Everyone knelt and pleaded, “He has gone mad with drink. Please forgive him, elder brother.” Song Jiang replied, “Worthy brothers, please rise. For now, put this brute under guard.” Everyone was delighted. Several guards charged with carrying out punishments came forward to take Li Kui away. Li Kui said, “Do you think I would dare resist? If my elder brother kills me, I will bear no grudge; if he cuts me to pieces, I will feel no hatred. Apart from him, I fear not even Heaven.” With that, he followed the guards to the prison room and went to sleep. Hearing his words, Song Jiang suddenly sobered up and was overcome with sorrow. Wu Yong urged him, “Elder brother, you arranged this gathering so that everyone might drink and make merry. He is a rough and reckless fellow who offended you in a moment of drunkenness. Why take it to heart? Stay and enjoy the occasion with all our brothers.” Song Jiang said, “When I was drunk in Jiangzhou, I mistakenly composed a seditious poem, and it was through his strength that I escaped. Today I composed another lyric to ‘The River All Red’ and very nearly cost him his life! Fortunately, all our brothers remonstrated and saved him. Of all men, he and I share the deepest bond. That is why my tears began to flow.” Then he called to Wu Song, “Brother, you are a man who understands affairs. I advocate accepting amnesty so that we may abandon wrongdoing, return to the right path, and become servants of the state. How would that chill everyone’s heart?” Lu Zhishen said, “The court is now full of civil and military officials who are mostly treacherous and wicked, and they obscure the sagacious understanding of His Majesty. It is like my robe being dyed black—however fiercely you wash it, how could it ever come clean? If amnesty proves useless, I will take my leave. Tomorrow let each of us go his own way and seek his fortune.” Song Jiang said, “Brothers, hear me. Our present Emperor is supremely wise and enlightened. It is only because treacherous ministers have blocked the channels of truth that his judgment is clouded for a time. One day the clouds will part and the sun appear. He will learn that we act on Heaven’s behalf and do not trouble innocent people; then he will pardon our crimes and offer us amnesty. United in serving the country, we shall leave our names in history—what could be finer? That is the only reason I wish us to accept amnesty soon. I have no other intention.” Everyone repeatedly expressed his gratitude. Yet their drinking that day never became truly joyous. When the feast ended, each returned to his own stronghold.

p.src: Nothing happened for some time, and the year gradually drew to its close. One day, after a long spell of snow had finally cleared, a man came up from below the mountain to report that seven or eight li from the stronghold they had captured a party escorting lanterns from Laizhou to the Eastern Capital, and the prisoners were waiting outside the pass for orders. Song Jiang said, “Do not bind them. Treat them well and bring them through the pass.” Before long they were brought before the hall: two constables, eight or nine lantern makers, and five carts. The leader reported, “I am a constable commissioned by Laizhou, and these men are all lantern makers. Every year the Eastern Capital orders our prefecture to provide three lantern structures. This year it added two more, namely these exquisite ninefold flower lanterns with jade frames.” Song Jiang at once gave them food and wine, then ordered the lanterns taken out for inspection. The craftsmen hung up the jade-framed lantern, fastening its ties on all four sides. From top to bottom it held nine times nine, eighty-one lights; suspended from the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, it reached all the way to the ground. Song Jiang said, “I had thought of keeping all of you here, but I fear it would bring you hardship and would not be proper or prudent. I shall keep only this ninefold flower lantern here. You may escort the others to the authorities yourselves. For your trouble, here are twenty taels of silver.” The men bowed twice and thanked him profusely before descending the mountain.

The next day he said to the assembled chieftains, “I was born and raised in Shandong and have never visited the capital. I hear that the present Emperor has put up a magnificent display of lanterns to rejoice with the people and celebrate the Lantern Festival. Work on the lanterns began just after the winter solstice, and they have only now been completed. Now I intend to go secretly with several brothers to see the lanterns, and then return at once.” Wu Yong remonstrated, “You must not! The Eastern Capital is now full of constables. What are we to do if something goes wrong?” Song Jiang said, “By day I shall remain hidden in an inn, and by night I shall enter the city to view the lanterns. What is there to fear?” Though everyone earnestly tried to dissuade him, Song Jiang could not be stopped and remained determined to go.
